blocks.text: You have ideas and you want to do them, but you keep postponing — "The quality is still low, so I can't show this to people yet" "I'll publish it once I'm more perfectly prepared" — and in the meantime, your enthusiasm cools, or someone else gets ahead of you.
Are you troubled by that "dilemma of not being able to shape anything because of perfectionism"?
A Finished 60-Point Product Is Worth More Than an Unfinished 100-Point One

As a matter of how the world works, no matter how perfect a plan you build in your head, until you put it out into the world once, see people's reactions, and actually run it, you won't even see the next points to improve.
"First, shape it, even if it's incomplete (Done is better than perfect)." That clear-eyed acceptance is the only driving force that dynamically moves reality.
Wisdom That Pushes Your Back Toward "Starting Small"
When your hands have stopped because of perfectionism, you open DECIDE. and draw a card.

When you read thoughtful encouragement like "Let go of the fine details for now, and prioritize shaping the whole thing first," you can take a light step forward: "All right — even if it's clumsy, let me put out today's part."
Let's shed the heavy armor called perfection, and experience the joy of shaping things lightly.

articles.title: Letting go of the pressure to 'become somebody.' A perspective for living comfortably as your true, ordinary self
articles.summary: When you look at social media, people who succeeded young and people shining with special talents keep catching your eye. Do you ever feel driven by impatience, thinking, "I have to leave some special achievement and become 'somebody' recognized by the world..."?

blocks.text: When you look at social media, people who succeeded young and people shining with special talents keep catching your eye. Do you ever feel driven by impatience, thinking, "I have to leave some special achievement and become 'somebody' recognized by the world"?
That impatience becomes too strong, and your own modest daily life and your happiness just as you are start to look faded.
Your Life Is Precious Enough Without Becoming a Special "Somebody"
The pressure we chase — "I have to become somebody" — is usually born from illusions created by the world and comparisons with others.

Not everyone needs to become an influencer or a business owner. Carefully savoring the daily life in front of you, treasuring the people who matter to you, and living in good spirits at your own pace. That itself is already a way of living with the highest value.
A Quiet Reset Time to Return to Your True Self
When you're tired from stretching yourself to become someone special, open DECIDE. and make time to bring your awareness back to your true self.

The messages a card offers you never tell you to "become something special." They quietly teach you the importance of what's at your feet: "As you are now, how do you make a choice you can be satisfied with?"
Why not have time to stop stretching yourself, and to supplely love your true self?

articles.title: Turning a vague anxiety into energy: steps for structured thinking
articles.summary: As you spend your days carrying vague anxiety about the future and haziness about work, you fall into a feeling as if your energy is being drained all day long. Because you don't know specifically what the problem is, there's no way to take countermeasures...

blocks.text: As you spend your days carrying vague anxiety about the future and haziness about work, you fall into a feeling as if your energy is being drained all day long. Because you don't know specifically what the problem is, there's no way to take countermeasures.
Are you experiencing that feeling, as if you've wandered into a "fog with no visible shape"?
Structure Your Anxiety and Break It Down into Controllable Problems

The biggest reason people feel fear is that a problem looks like something "huge and uncontrollable." But if you can unravel that fog and neatly sort (structure) it into "things I can do something about right now" and "things I can't do anything about," your anxiety becomes surprisingly small.
An excellent catalyst for smoothly doing that sorting work is right here.
Neatly Organize the Haziness with a Card's Framework
You draw a card in DECIDE., and while reading the hint presented, you write out in a notebook, "What am I most stuck on right now?"
From the moment you can structure it — "I can control this part, so I'll deal with it tomorrow; this part is overthinking, so I'll let it go" — anxiety is reborn as "concrete tasks to do today."
Let's put an end to standing still in the fog, and clear your field of vision with your own hands.

articles.title: 'Choosing again is not failure.' The flexible career that comes from adjusting your course with ease
articles.summary: "Since I decided on this path once, I have to see it through to the end, no matter what." "Changing direction midway feels embarrassing, as if I'm admitting my planning mistake or a setback."

blocks.text: "Since I decided on this path once, I have to see it through to the end, no matter what." "Changing direction midway feels embarrassing, as if I'm admitting my planning mistake or a setback."
Have you ever, out of that earnestness, forced yourself to keep going while feeling something was off, and worn yourself down both physically and mentally?
Update the Curse of "Three Years on a Stone"

In today's rapidly changing world, "seeing everything through exactly as you first planned" is not always considered a virtue. The flexibility to quickly correct your direction when, after actually moving forward, you realize "this wasn't the direction I should go" — that is the strongest weapon for living a long life supplely.
Stopping once and choosing again is by no means a setback — it's a wise update for a better future.
A Thoughtful Partner That Gently Tells You When to Correct Course
When you're unsure, "Should I continue with my current approach, or should I change direction?" you open DECIDE. and draw a card.

If a hint appears there — "It's time to let go of past attachments and choose a new route" — that's the best timing to boldly turn the rudder. Rely on your intuition and objective wisdom, and lightly correct your course.
Why not treasure the flexibility to choose your future again, supplely, without clinging too much to a single path?

articles.title: A prescription for days when things just don't go well. The quiet art of lowering expectations and carrying on calmly
articles.summary: From the morning, things just don't seem to mesh — you make a mistake replying to an email, spill your coffee, get irritated over small things. "Today just isn't my day, all day long." Have you ever had a day like that...

blocks.text: From the morning, things just don't seem to mesh — you make a mistake replying to an email, spill your coffee, get irritated over small things. "Today just isn't my day, all day long." Have you ever had a day like that?
And on days like that, you try to make up for it, telling yourself you have to try harder, and only end up spinning your wheels and making things worse.
On an unlucky day, lower the bar for effort — a lot

In life, there are days when you can go full throttle and get results, and days when, for some reason, your energy just doesn't line up. On those days, the best answer is not to force a comeback, but to accept it cleanly — "today is just a low-energy day" — and lower your expectations.
Get through the day calmly, handling only the minimum tasks, without causing a major mishap. That alone makes the day a perfect score.
A switch for deciding, "I'll go in energy-saving mode today"
On a day when everything feels like it might spin out of control, open DECIDE., draw a card, and check in on your current condition.

"Today is not a day for moving things in a big way overall, but a day to steady your footing and spend it quietly." When you see a message like that, you can switch your mindset cleanly: "All right, today I'll take it easy and save energy."
On days when you're not at your best, let's have the wisdom to lower expectations considerably and let the day pass calmly.

articles.title: Freeing yourself from the illusion of other people's evaluations. A lesson for the heart on living for yourself
articles.summary: Whether buying new clothes or speaking up at work, you shrink back, worrying excessively about what others will think: "What will that person think of me?" "What if I stand out in a strange way and people talk badly about me?"

blocks.text: Whether buying new clothes or speaking up at work, you shrink back, worrying excessively about what others will think: "What will that person think of me?" "What if I stand out in a strange way and people talk badly about me?"
Even though you are supposed to be living your own life, have you become unable to move inside an invisible cage called "evaluation by others"?
Other people are not watching you as much as you think

When we feel "afraid of others' eyes," an excessive assumption is at work in our brains: "Everyone is closely monitoring and evaluating my actions." But in reality, other people are each at full capacity with their own matters, and do not pay that much deep attention to other people's actions.
It is far too wasteful to hold back from what you want to do, frightened by the phantom of other people's evaluations.
Personal time to reclaim choices made for yourself
When you become unable to move because you are worried about others' eyes, open DECIDE. and refocus your awareness on your own inner self.
What the card you draw there shows is neither other people's evaluations nor society's common sense, but only the pure theme of "how you yourself want to be right now."
Why not step out of the cage of worrying too much about others' eyes, and taste the joy of living more freely, for yourself?

articles.title: A small step can change the future in a big way. Steady habits built up, rather than dramatic change
articles.summary: Wanting to change your life completely and grow more, you make plans with hurdles that are far too high from the start — "From next month, I'll study for 2 hours every day!" "I'll completely renew my lifestyle habits!" — and then give up after just a few days...

blocks.text: Wanting to change your life completely and grow more, you make plans with hurdles that are far too high from the start — "From next month, I'll study for 2 hours every day!" "I'll completely renew my lifestyle habits!" — and then give up after just a few days.
Do you keep repeating that "loop of aiming for extreme change and failing"?
What changes your life is not a dramatic event, but plain, everyday choices

Our future does not change in a single dramatic, movie-like moment. The accumulation of actions lasting just a few minutes, and small habits of thought, that we choose in our daily lives is what shapes our reality a few months or a few years from now.
That is why what you should change is not a big goal, but "the quality of the small choices you make in this very moment."
Three minutes a day: a habit for raising the quality of small choices
DECIDE. is the smartest companion for raising that "quality of everyday small choices" without strain, and settling it in as a reliable habit.

Once a day, face a quiet screen, draw a card, organize your thoughts, and leave them in your log. That plain, everyday accumulation, before you know it, will take you to a wonderful place you never imagined.
Instead of dreaming of a big change, let's carefully build up today's step, one at a time.

articles.title: Moving on from just drifting through life. A nighttime strategy session to return as the protagonist of your own life
articles.summary: Before you know it, a week has simply passed by, and you can't even remember what you accomplished or what moved you. Have you ever felt that emptiness at night, as if you were watching a highlight reel of your own life as someone else's story...

blocks.text: Before you know it, a week has simply passed by, and you can't even remember what you accomplished or what moved you. Have you ever felt that emptiness at night, as if you were watching a highlight reel of your own life as someone else's story?
When we are drowning in busyness, we can easily slip into becoming mere passengers in our own lives.
From a passive "guest" to an active "main character"
To take firm hold of the lead in your life again and live as the main character of your own story, what you need is a short time at night for a "strategy meeting with yourself."
Design, by your own will, how to give meaning to today and how to meet tomorrow.
A life strategy meeting, held in a quiet study
In the calm time before sleep, open DECIDE., reflect on today's choices, and draw a card.

While savoring the hint shown there, make a small plan: "For the next few days, I'll spend my time keeping this theme in mind." Those few minutes of proactive approach can turn passive days into a vivid drama.
Let's graduate from passive days and, starting today, return to being the main character of your own life.

articles.title: 'Hesitating is not a bad thing.' Time spent wavering as proof that you are taking your own life seriously
articles.summary: When you are faced with a big choice, have you ever blamed yourself while worrying, thinking, "Why am I so indecisive?" or "I'm a hopeless person for not being able to decide quickly"?

blocks.text: When you are faced with a big choice, have you ever blamed yourself while worrying, thinking, "Why am I so indecisive?" or "I'm a hopeless person for not being able to decide quickly"?
Influenced by the atmosphere in society that says "quick decisions are always right," you end up feeling ashamed of the very state of being undecided.
Worrying means you are facing it seriously
But think about it. People never keep worrying for days over something they don't care about, or something that has no value to them at all.

The reason you are worrying and struggling so much right now is precisely because you sincerely wish to "be honest with your own life and the people involved, and find a better answer." Worrying is not a flaw at all — it is the clearest proof that you are facing your life earnestly.
Turn time spent worrying into "a precious process for knowing yourself deeply"
DECIDE. never denies or rushes that "time you spend seriously worrying."
Rather, it stays close to the depth of your uncertainty and gently continues to support the process until you arrive at your own answer, through the rich wisdom of 78 cards and quiet dialogue.
Why not stop blaming yourself for worrying, and fully savor that time of careful thought?

articles.title: Putting an end to nights when you can't sleep from overthinking. A way to let circling thoughts out and rest your brain
articles.summary: You got into bed and closed your eyes, but a small conversation from the day, or trouble next week that hasn't even happened yet, starts going round and round in your head, and before you know it the clock is pointing to the middle of the night. Do you spend such "nights when you can't sleep because you're thinking too much"...

blocks.text: You got into bed and closed your eyes, but a small conversation from the day, or trouble next week that hasn't even happened yet, starts going round and round in your head, and before you know it the clock is pointing to the middle of the night. Do you spend such "nights when you can't sleep because you're thinking too much"?

At night, compared to the daytime, the brain's logical brakes don't work as well, and it tends to amplify and reproduce only emotions and anxieties. In other words, no matter how seriously you worry in bed, a good solution will almost never come out of it.
Move your thoughts from inside your head to "on the screen"

The best way to stop looping thoughts is to convince your brain, "I've decided to stop thinking about this matter." To do that, it helps to take the unease in your head out into the outside world once, attach a tentative conclusion to it, and save it.
As an emergency shelter for such sleepless nights, I use DECIDE..
Use one card to draw a line: "That's enough for tonight"

Open the quiet screen, gentle on the eyes even in a dark room, and draw one card on the theme that is occupying your head right now. Then read the calm hint written there, decide, "All right, I'll think about this again tomorrow morning based on this perspective," leave just one line in the log, and close the screen.
When your brain feels reassured — "I've recorded it in the log, so it's okay to forget it now" — the tension eases, and you can fall into sleep surprisingly calmly.
When you get caught in a nighttime loop of thoughts, instead of carrying it alone, why not entrust your burden to a quiet card?

articles.title: For those who want to do too many things and end up doing none of them fully. How to choose so your passion gathers in one place
articles.summary: You buy several books you're interested in at once, take an interest in new studies, and hold multiple work projects. Having a strong curiosity is wonderful, but have you ever spread yourself too thin, this and that, and ended up leaving everything half-finished...

blocks.text: You buy several books you're interested in at once, take an interest in new studies, and hold multiple work projects. Having a strong curiosity is wonderful, but have you ever spread yourself too thin, this and that, and ended up leaving everything half-finished and falling into self-loathing?
Since our time and energy are limited, it is impossible to move everything forward at the same time.
To "do it all," decide the order
When you have several things you want to do, you don't need to give something up and throw it away. You just need to decide the order — which one to shine the spotlight on at this very moment.
That said, precisely because each theme is attractive to you, you may find yourself unsure which to start with. That is exactly when DECIDE. comes in.
Start with the one that resonates with the card's theme
Draw one card in DECIDE., and compare the card's qualities and hints with the several things you want to do.

For example, if hints like "build your foundation" or "steady repetition" appear, your focus will naturally settle: rather than a flashy new project, let's start with the foundational study that builds your base.
When you focus the lens of your scattered passion onto a single point, things begin to take shape at a surprising speed. Why not decide, together with a card, where to shine today's spotlight?

articles.title: When opinions clash, how do you find common ground? A perspective for turning emotional conflict into constructive dialogue
articles.summary: When opinions split within a workplace team, or when you and your partner disagree about the future. "My way of thinking is absolutely right, so why won't the other person understand?" Have you ever exhausted yourself as the discussion goes in circles...

blocks.text: When opinions split within a workplace team, or when you and your partner disagree about the future. "My way of thinking is absolutely right, so why won't the other person understand?" Have you ever exhausted yourself as the discussion goes in circles?
When opinions clash, we tend to slip into a "win or lose" mode, nitpicking the other person's words and desperately trying to prove our own legitimacy.
From "who is right" to "how can we make it work"
What is needed to overcome a conflict is not to argue the other person down, but to find the "values we truly want to protect" behind each other's claims, and to look for a third landing point.
When my head is hot and my view has narrowed, I make it a habit to draw one card in DECIDE. before a conversation.
A calm hint, like a third party's, gives you an opening to meet halfway
The 78 hints DECIDE. shows open a window in a deadlocked situation, like a skilled facilitator.

"Rather than asserting your own rightness, first listen to the anxiety behind the other person's position." "Rather than mixing the two opinions together, create an entirely new framework." When you encounter words like these, your rigid heart softens, and the next words you offer the other person change gently.
To build a better agreement without breaking your relationship with someone important. Please try using a card as quiet preparation before a conversation.

articles.title: When you're torn between spending and saving. How to shop by your own values, not by price
articles.summary: Furniture or a gadget priced a little beyond your comfort zone, or a course for investing in yourself. You want it, but you wonder, "Will it really be worth the cost?" or "Will it just be a waste of money?" and your finger stops before pressing the payment button...

blocks.text: Furniture or a gadget priced a little beyond your comfort zone, or a course for investing in yourself. You want it, but you wonder, "Will it really be worth the cost?" or "Will it just be a waste of money?" and your finger stops before pressing the payment button — has that ever happened to you?

Conversely, it is also a common story that you hold back on spending, buy a cheap compromise, quickly stop using it, and regret it, thinking, "I should have just bought the one I really wanted from the start."
When you think in terms of "gain and loss" you get stuck; when you think in terms of "values" you can decide

When we are unsure about how to use money, we tend to try to judge only by calculations of gain and loss — "Is it a good deal?" "Will I fail?" But what decides whether that purchase is right for you is not general cost performance. It is only one thing: "Does it match the theme of your life right now?"
To see that essence clearly, I open DECIDE. before making a big purchase.
Use a card's question to check the "purity" of your reason for wanting it

Draw a card while picturing the thing you are unsure about buying, and read its hint. Then, sometimes you can calmly realize, "Ah, I don't really need this — I was just trying to buy it on impulse to release work stress." At other times, you can feel certain: "For me to move to the next stage right now, this investment is truly necessary."
When you start making sure of your own sense of conviction before paying, your satisfaction with your purchases becomes surprisingly higher.

articles.title: When you've paused on a landing in your career. How to calmly assess whether to stay in your current job or make a change
articles.summary: You don't have any decisive dissatisfaction with your current workplace, and you have learned to handle most of the work. But when you imagine yourself in three or five years, you wonder whether it is okay to stay in the same place, and you feel a sudden sense of the ground swaying beneath you...

blocks.text: You don't have any decisive dissatisfaction with your current workplace, and you have learned to handle most of the work. But when you imagine yourself in three or five years, you wonder whether it is okay to stay in the same place, and you feel a sudden sense of the ground swaying beneath you.

When we reach such a "career plateau," we tend to act in extremes — suddenly feeling anxious and browsing job change sites, or conversely stopping thinking about it and immersing ourselves in the work in front of us.
Before changing your environment, first learn the "true nature of your thirst"

When your current place feels boring, do you truly need to change the environment itself (change jobs), or would you be fulfilled by changing your "way of working and relating" within the current environment? If you misjudge that, you will repeat the same uncertainty even after changing places.
Ongoing dialogue with DECIDE. is very helpful for exploring where the thirst in your heart comes from.
Save small daily feelings of discomfort in a log and use them as material for a big decision

Big decisions like career choices, in particular, should not be answered in a single day. On days when work leaves you feeling unsettled, and on days when you feel a sense of fulfillment, draw a card with DECIDE. and leave your emotions in a log.

When you look back over several weeks of logs and statistics, unwavering facts come into view: "I feel the most stress from not having discretion," or "After all, I love work that creates new systems." Only once you understand that much can we make our next move without regret.

articles.title: Is your habit of searching right away taking away your ability to think? A three-minute habit to try before opening the search box
articles.summary: The moment a question or a moment of uncertainty arises, do you reflexively type keywords into your smartphone's search box? "XX job change regret," "Should I buy XX," "tired of relationships how to deal."

blocks.text: The moment a question or a moment of uncertainty arises, do you reflexively type keywords into your smartphone's search box? "XX job change regret," "Should I buy XX," "tired of relationships how to deal."

Of course, if you search, summary articles written by someone will come up right away. But if you always look only for "answers that are out there" from the start like that, the ability to think with your own head and feel with your own heart gradually weakens.
Other people's summary articles do not contain your context
Articles on the internet are, at best, "generalizations that fit the greatest common denominator." They take no account of your history so far, or of the delicate nuances of your feelings.
That is why, before you search and pour other people's opinions into your brain, it is important to insert just 3 minutes to listen to your own voice — "what do I think?"
Instead of a search engine, open a tool that connects you to your inner self
When I feel unsure about something and want to search, I open DECIDE. first, instead of the browser's search box.
DECIDE. is not a search engine that tells you the answer. Through its 78 cards, it is a place that throws the ball of thought back to you: "There is also this viewpoint — how do you feel about it?"

First think with your own head and come up with a tentative answer, and only then search for the information you need. Just by keeping that order, you will grow a strong sense of your own axis, unswayed by information.

articles.title: A way of living that doesn't rely on motivation. A switch to move yourself calmly, even on days when you don't feel like it
articles.summary: "I'll start when I feel motivated." "I'll wait until my motivation rises." If you think that way, your hands never move, no matter how much time passes. Everyone has had that experience.

blocks.text: "I'll start when I feel motivated." "I'll wait until my motivation rises." If you think that way, your hands never move, no matter how much time passes. Everyone has had that experience.

In the first place, motivation is nothing more than an emotion that fluctuates capriciously, like the weather or the temperature. If you entrust your daily actions to something so unstable, continuing anything becomes extremely difficult.
You don't move because you're motivated — you become motivated because you move
In the world of brain science, it is known that the motivation switch does not exist "before you start acting," but only turns on "after you have started moving your hands anyway."
In other words, what you need on a day when you don't feel like it is not hot words to fire yourself up, but a small ritual (trigger) for entering work mode calmly, without emotion.
Make the act of drawing a card your signal to start acting
For me, DECIDE. has become the "ritual" before I start work or tasks.

When I sit at my desk and feel somehow heavy-hearted, I open DECIDE. without thinking and draw one card. Then I read the hint displayed there in 15 seconds, decide, "All right, I'll just keep this perspective in mind and move my hands for the first 10 minutes," and get to work.
Regardless of whether you have motivation or not, when you draw a card, your hands move automatically. Why not create such a comfortable switch of your own in your daily life?

articles.title: Overcoming the fear of deciding for yourself. Regaining control of your life through small exercises in self-determination
articles.summary: When you have to decide something, you freeze, thinking, "What if I make a mistake and someone blames me?" "I'm afraid of taking responsibility myself," and you end up handing the decision over to others, saying "I'm fine with the same as everyone else" or "I'll leave it to you"...

blocks.text: When you have to decide something, you freeze, thinking, "What if I make a mistake and someone blames me?" "I'm afraid of taking responsibility myself," and you end up handing the decision over to others, saying "I'm fine with the same as everyone else" or "I'll leave it to you."

Getting through things that way without making waves is temporarily easier, but if you keep doing it, you can fall into a feeling that, even though it's your own life, there is nowhere in it where you belong.
The fear of deciding comes from "trying to lift a heavy load all at once"

People who are afraid to decide for themselves take decisions too heavily, as "a grave responsibility that determines their life." If you try to lift a heavy barbell all at once without any muscle strength, it's only natural to be afraid of getting hurt.
What matters is to start your rehabilitation in deciding for yourself with "ultra-lightweight choices" that won't trouble anyone and won't hurt at all even if you fail.
Practice deciding in a safe place where no one is watching
DECIDE. is, for exactly that rehabilitation, a space that could not be safer or quieter.

"Which book should I start reading on today's day off?" "With what attitude should I listen in this afternoon's meeting?" Draw a card on such a small theme, read the hint, decide for yourself, "All right, I'll do it this way," and leave it in the log.
That accumulation of small self-decisions, which no one grades, will little by little nurture in your heart a solid confidence: "It's okay for me to decide for myself."

articles.title: When it's time to let go of past glory and old ways of doing things. Tidying your mind to update to a new version of yourself
articles.summary: The way of working that once went well for you, or a role you were praised for in the past. Those are important achievements that have supported you, but if you cling to "old patterns of success" even though times and circumstances have changed, they can, before you know it, become shackles that hinder your growth...

blocks.text: The way of working that once went well for you, or a role you were praised for in the past. Those are important achievements that have supported you, but if you cling to "old patterns of success" even though times and circumstances have changed, they can, before you know it, become shackles that hinder your growth.

Even though you understand in your head, "It's about time I changed my approach," letting go of a style you've been familiar with for years feels a little lonely and frightening, as if you were losing a part of yourself.
Letting go is not denying your past self

When you graduate from a familiar way of doing things or environment, what matters is not to think, "I'm throwing it away because my old way was wrong," but to hold the feeling, "I'm grateful it brought me this far, and now I'll change into equipment for the next stage."
Quietly supporting that mental shift is the idea of "cycles" held by tarot's 78 cards.
The natural metabolism the cards' stories teach us
As you draw cards in DECIDE., you are made aware that things have a natural rhythm: "a beginning, growth, fruition, and then being broken down once so new seeds can be sown."

If, when you are feeling stuck right now, you encounter a card that suggests letting go or renewal, it is like a warm diploma saying, "You've done enough, so you can move on to the next stage with peace of mind."
Why not borrow the wisdom of the cards to update yourself lightly to a new version of you, while affirming your past self?

articles.title: Honoring the feeling that 'putting it into words makes it sound untrue.' How to scoop up delicate true feelings without breaking them
articles.summary: There is certainly some important feeling or unease in your heart, but the moment you try to force it into easy-to-understand words to explain to someone else, or organize it in bullet points in a notebook, you feel, "Somehow this has become something thin and different from my real feelings..."

blocks.text: There is certainly some important feeling or unease in your heart, but the moment you try to force it into easy-to-understand words to explain to someone else, or organize it in bullet points in a notebook, you feel, "Somehow this has become something thin and different from my real feelings." Have you ever felt that?

Our emotions and true feelings are originally very delicate, rich in gradation. If you try to scoop them up with the coarse net of existing words like "positive / negative" or "for / against," the most important nuances spill out and are lost.
Instead of putting it directly into words, borrow the power of symbols

When dealing with delicate feelings that are hard to put into words, the world of psychology and art often uses a method of avoiding direct verbalization and going through "pictures and stories (symbols)" instead.
The abstract, profound worldview held by tarot's 78 cards is precisely a vessel for receiving, just as they are, those "delicate true feelings from before they become words."
Hints with room to breathe affirm your feelings just as they are
That is also why DECIDE.'s text is written avoiding a strongly assertive tone that settles things in black and white, leaving a somewhat poetic, intelligent space.

Gazing at the card and hint shown on the screen, you feel, "Yes, that's it — I couldn't put it into words, but my feeling right now is very close to the atmosphere of this card." Even without forcing yourself into an easy-to-understand conclusion, just finding a place where your feelings resonate like that deeply saves your heart.

Why not step a little away from an everyday life where everything must be explained logically, and taste the comfort of entrusting your heart to the space within symbols?

articles.summary: Social media, where you once could casually post everyday thoughts and uncertainties, has at some point changed into a place where you are conscious of algorithms and other people's eyes. Many people unconsciously censor themselves before posting, thinking, "What will people think if I write something like this?" or...

blocks.text: Social media, where you once could casually post everyday thoughts and uncertainties, has at some point changed into a place where you are conscious of algorithms and other people's eyes. Many people unconsciously censor themselves before posting, thinking, "What will people think if I write something like this?" or "Maybe I shouldn't put out negative things."
As a reaction to that, the value of "closed places" where no one else's eyes enter at all — such as locked accounts and paper diaries — is now being reconsidered.
Your true voice can only come out in a place that doesn't need "likes"

Writing that assumes it will be read by someone inevitably mixes in a little "stretching yourself" or "posing." But when we are truly uncertain and make a decision while facing our own weakness and dishonesty, other people's eyes and "like" evaluations only get in the way.
What you need is a completely closed digital study of your own, connected to no one else in the world.
The comfort of a "log" where you purely store your own thoughts

DECIDE. has no timeline premised on sharing like social media, and no function to see other people's posts. The card you drew and the "log" of the uncertainty and decision you thought about at that time quietly accumulate solely for you to look back on yourself.
Precisely because you know no one will see it, you can write surprisingly honest, unadorned true feelings there.
If you feel a little tired of posting in open spaces, why not nurture a log of your own thoughts in this quiet place where no one's evaluation enters?

articles.title: Escaping the labyrinth of searching for what you want to do. A way of living guided by today's small discomforts, rather than a grand passion
articles.summary: "Let's find what you truly want to do, something you can devote your life to." Every time you encounter words like that, do you ever feel inferior about yourself for not having something you can hold such strong passion for?

blocks.text: "Let's find what you truly want to do, something you can devote your life to." Every time you encounter words like that, do you ever feel inferior about yourself for not having something you can hold such strong passion for?

Even if you read self-analysis books or review your past, a "calling" or "dream" you'd throw everything away to chase is not so easily found, and in the end you spend years treading water in the labyrinth of searching for what you want to do.
Rather than searching for a "strong passion," gather your "small comforts and discomforts"

In fact, only a very small number of people have a clear "thing they want to do" from the start. For most people, a path that feels like their own is something that only becomes visible in hindsight, as the result of continuing to choose in daily life according to subtle sensors: "This feels somehow pleasant," or "This feels a little off."
In other words, there is no need to search for a grand dream — you just need to raise the "precision of today's small choices."
Sharpen your heart's sensor with a daily card draw
DECIDE. is a tool like a magnifying glass for picking up such subtle sensations in everyday life.

Draw a card for the small moments of indecision that arise day by day, observe how your heart stirs when you read the hint presented, and leave it in the log. When you look back on that accumulation through the statistics feature, an outline naturally emerges: "I'm the kind of person who prefers this kind of environment and way of working."
Why not put the grand search for what you want to do on hold for once, and start by truly accepting the small choice in front of you today?

articles.title: Saving a brain chased by multitasking and notifications. Three minutes of mindfulness to face your own heart through single-tasking
articles.summary: While making materials on your computer you reply to a chat tool, and when your smartphone notification rings you look there too. We today are constantly placed in a state of "multitasking," handling multiple things at the same time...

blocks.text: While making materials on your computer you reply to a chat tool, and when your smartphone notification rings you look there too. We today are constantly placed in a state of "multitasking," handling multiple things at the same time.

However, from a brain science perspective, it is said that humans cannot multitask in the true sense, and are merely switching the target of attention at extremely high speed. That is precisely why, by evening, our brains end up exhausted as if they have overheated.
For modern people who are not good at closing their eyes and meditating

As a way to relieve brain fatigue, "mindfulness (meditation)" is often recommended, but for those of us usually surrounded by information, suddenly closing our eyes and trying to become "empty" can be difficult, with distracting thoughts welling up instead.
Rather than that, creating "single-task time" where you concentrate your awareness on just one beautiful object can calm your mind much more smoothly.
Dynamic mindfulness — directing your awareness to just one card
The DECIDE. screen is designed precisely for this "concentrating on just one thing."

Open the quiet screen with no unnecessary notifications or ads, picture just one current theme of yours, and draw a card. Then, direct all of your awareness for three minutes only to the one card that appeared on the screen and the words of the hint written there.
The scattered tabs in your brain close one by one, and by the time you finish using it, a quietness like after taking a deep breath returns to your mind.

articles.title: The trap hidden in shopping and choosing so you never fail. How to invite serendipity that breaks the predictable
articles.summary: When you enter a restaurant you always check the number of stars on a review site beforehand, when you watch a movie you read spoiler-free reviews before buying a ticket, and when you buy clothes you choose classic colors that are easy to mix and match.

blocks.text: When you enter a restaurant you always check the number of stars on a review site beforehand, when you watch a movie you read spoiler-free reviews before buying a ticket, and when you buy clothes you choose classic colors that are easy to mix and match.

In today's world where prices have risen and time is limited, it is a very natural psychology to become cautious, thinking, "I absolutely don't want to fail or lose out." But the more we try to make failure zero, doesn't the "unexpected emotion" also disappear from life?
With choices based on avoiding deductions, a future beyond expectations will not come

If you only choose "not failing" through advance research, our everyday life becomes a repetition of predictable harmony you have seen somewhere before. What truly makes life interesting is always an encounter beyond calculation — in other words, "serendipity (accidental good fortune)."
That said, it is frightening to suddenly take a reckless gamble in real shopping or work. That is precisely why we first try bringing safe chance into the "process of thinking."
78 cards bring an unplanned new perspective
Drawing a card with DECIDE. is an act of inviting pleasant serendipity into your own rigid "calculations to avoid failure."

A card randomly presents an approach you would never have chosen on your own, or a perspective you had overlooked. By going along with that chance hint, you can lightly step beyond the frame of predictable harmony, thinking, "I would usually take the safe option, but this time I might try this new way."
Why not step out from honor-student choices that merely avoid failure, and enjoy the new scenery that chance brings?

articles.title: For modern people with many faces — parallel career, family, personal life — a card habit as a switch for changing modes
articles.summary: The face of a businessperson in your main job, the face of a creator advancing a side job or personal project, and when you return home, the face of a parent or partner. Those of us living today switch between several different roles in the course of a single day…

blocks.text: The face of a businessperson in your main job, the face of a creator advancing a side job or personal project, and when you return home, the face of a parent or partner. Those of us living today live while switching between several different roles (personas) in the course of a single day.

Having multiple worlds enriches life, but on the other hand, it also tends to create uncertainty: you carry the fatigue and mode of thinking from the previous role straight into the next part of your day, and your head doesn't switch over well.
Because physical movement has disappeared, the heart needs a "ticket gate"
Especially now, when opportunities to work and do tasks at home have increased, in the few steps between closing your computer and going to the living room, your brain's mode doesn't switch easily.
To move from work mode to personal mode, or from everyday chores to creative thinking, you need a "ritual (switch)" that consciously changes your brain's channel.
Setting the stance of your next self by drawing a single card
At the timing when I switch roles, I always open DECIDE. and draw a single card.

For example, I draw a card after finishing my main job and before starting on my own project. By reading the hint written there, the "self who moves by the logic of the organization" from the daytime is reset for a moment, and I can slip smoothly into my new-mode self: "All right — for this time from here on, I'll face my own expression with this stance."
Why not keep quiet cards in your pocket as a "ticket gate for the heart," for moving lightly between your many roles?

articles.title: In a social media age full of takedowns and extremes, how to protect a gray zone — a margin — inside yourself
articles.summary: When you open the comment sections of online news or social media, for any complex problem you see only strong extreme arguments like "A is absolutely right, B is completely wrong," and words that seem to argue someone down.

blocks.text: When you open the comment sections of online news or social media, for any complex problem you see only strong extreme arguments like "A is absolutely right, B is completely wrong," and words that seem to argue someone down.

Because such black-and-white words are highly stimulating, if you keep looking at them, our thinking too becomes influenced without us realizing it, and we may judge our own uncertainty in extremes — "success or failure," "do it or quit" — and make ourselves suffer.
Adult intelligence is being able to handle "gradations" without forcing black and white

In real life and human relationships, 100% white or 100% black hardly exists. "I want to do it, but I also feel anxious" "What the other person says has a point, but I can't accept it right away." The ability to hold such wavering gray zones as they are, without rushing to cut them away (negative capability), is precisely the intelligence of a mature adult.
To reclaim that space in my heart, I trust the worldview of DECIDE. very much.
Hints that do not assert definitively restore flexibility of thought

The words that appear when you draw a card with DECIDE. contain none of the strong assertions or extreme arguments flying around on social media. Based on both sides of things — light and shadow, upright and reversed — it presents a rich gradation, saying, "Right now, there is also this way of finding balance."
When you encounter that calm, intelligent writing, your sharp heart relaxes and settles, thinking, "I see, I don't have to force black and white right now — I can look for this middle path."
When you are tired of extreme arguments, open this quiet page to protect a rich gray zone in your own heart.

articles.title: Well-being doesn't mean always being in a good mood. How to make decisions while living well alongside negative emotions too
articles.summary: In recent years, we have come to hear the words "well-being," referring to a state of being fulfilled in both body and mind, and "self-esteem" quite often. They are very lovely concepts, but if you interpret them as "you must always be positive, in a good mood, and live looking forward"...

blocks.text: In recent years, we have come to hear the words "well-being," referring to a state of being fulfilled in both body and mind, and "self-esteem" quite often. They are very lovely concepts, but if you interpret them as "you must always be positive, in a good mood, and live looking forward," they can instead become a new source of pressure.
That is because, being human, there are inevitably days when your mood sinks, and nights when your heart is unsettled with jealousy or impatience.
Don't make negative emotions the "villain"

True well-being is not forcibly erasing negative emotions, but a state where you can flatly acknowledge your own condition, including negative feelings — "Ah, I'm impatient right now," "I'm a little hurt" — and, on that basis, make a choice that is kind to yourself.
What is excellent about tarot's 78 cards is that they give equal citizenship not only to human joy and hope, but also to "shadow emotions" such as conflict, loss, and indecision.
A place that accepts you, in whatever mood, just as you are
When your mood is down, reading glittering self-help words can make it even harder, can't it? But DECIDE. is different.

No matter how negative your mood when you draw a card, it does not deny that state, but offers an intellectual hint that stays close to you as you are now: "Right now, rather than forcing yourself to look forward, the best choice is to heal your wounds and spend your time quietly."
If you're tired of forcing yourself to act positive, why not take a deep breath in this place, where you can gently hold hands with your negative self as well?

articles.title: Stepping back from the anxiety of reskilling and investing in yourself. A compass for discerning the learning you truly need now
articles.summary: "Reskilling to survive the AI era." "Adult relearning." Pushed forward by such words, or perhaps a little threatened by them, you sign up for qualification studies or online courses, but in the end your motivation doesn't last and they end up piling up like unread books...

blocks.text: "Reskilling to survive the AI era." "Adult relearning." Pushed forward by such words, or perhaps a little threatened by them, you sign up for qualification studies or online courses, but in the end your motivation doesn't last — do you have anything that has ended up piling up like a stack of unread books (tsundoku)?
The attitude of trying to learn is itself very admirable, but self-investment fueled by anxiety and fear — "If I don't acquire something, I'll be left behind" — inevitably runs out of breath midway.
"Skills the world demands" and "themes you yourself want to deepen"

What we, with our limited time and money, should truly invest in is not a skill chosen because "it's trending in the world," but "learning that is deeply connected to your current challenges and intellectual curiosity."
Before buying a new book or signing up for a course, please try using DECIDE. as a cushion to check whether it truly comes from your current honest feelings.
Through the card's perspective, make the "motivation" for learning clear

Draw one card on the theme "Should I start this study?" and read the hint. Then, sometimes you may be startled — "Isn't now a time to hone the skills you already have through practice, rather than cramming in new knowledge from outside?" — and at other times you may be powerfully encouraged — "That new field will be the key to breaking through your current stagnation."
To stop spreading yourself blindly out of impatience, and to invest in yourself truly convinced — "This is why I am learning this now." Why not start with three minutes of introspection?

articles.title: Closing work for the brain to improve sleep quality. From idly scrolling in blue light to three minutes of quiet reflection
articles.summary: The importance of sleep is being emphasized, and many people are making efforts to improve the quality of their sleep, such as changing their pillow or holding back on caffeine. But what many know is the biggest obstacle, yet find hard to stop, is idly looking at a smartphone in bed...

blocks.text: The importance of sleep is being emphasized, and many people are making efforts to improve the quality of their sleep, such as changing their pillow or holding back on caffeine. But what many know is the biggest obstacle, yet find hard to stop, is idly looking at a smartphone in bed, isn't it?

The reason you look at your phone even though you're sleepy is that your brain, having been chased by work and housework all day and unable to have "time just for yourself," tries to reclaim a little of its own time before sleeping (revenge bedtime procrastination) and keeps searching for stimulation.
Tell your brain, "Today has properly ended"

To stop revenge bedtime procrastination and fall into a comfortable sleep, it is important not simply to take the smartphone away, but to give your brain the satisfaction that "Today, too, I properly faced my own feelings, and the day is truly complete."
In other words, it is a "closing operation for the brain," like closing the register at a shop.
Close the day quietly on a dark-toned screen that is gentle on the eyes
At night, instead of opening a social media timeline, I make it my rule before sleeping to open DECIDE.'s calm screen.
While reflecting on the day's events, draw one card, read the quiet hint, and record today's decisions and feelings in the log in just one line. This takes only about three minutes.

Unlike watching stimulating videos or news, by putting your inner self in order and placing a period that says "recorded," your brain feels deeply satisfied, and you can put down your smartphone and fall asleep smoothly. Why not try a new habit before sleep, starting tonight?

articles.title: To remain a sustainable self. Small daily course corrections to prevent burnout
articles.summary: The word "sustainable" has come to be used for the environment and society, but this perspective may be exactly what we need most for our own ways of working and living.

blocks.text: The word "sustainable" has come to be used for the environment and society, but this perspective may be exactly what we need most for our own ways of working and living.

If you continue at an unreasonable pace on a strong sense of responsibility or temporary spirit alone, one day you may suddenly find you cannot get up in the morning, or cannot feel motivation for anything — you meet "burnout."
Instead of resting after you reach your limit, correct small misalignments every day

People who burn out tend to keep running without noticing until the meter of their heart turns red (the limit). The secret to continuing to run for a long time in a good mood is, at the stage when the meter is about to turn yellow, to notice "Ah, I'm pushing myself a little," and make fine adjustments to slow your pace frequently.
As a system for that daily condition check, DECIDE.'s logs and statistics are very helpful.
The history of cards you've drawn will tell you about your "overdoing it"
When you draw a card in DECIDE. every day or once every few days and record your state, you can objectively see in what situations you tend to push yourself.

Each time you encounter hints from the cards such as "rest," "letting go," and "temperance," you release the tension that had unconsciously entered your shoulders and make a small course correction: "This week I'll reduce my schedule a little and return to a sustainable pace."
The kinder someone is, the more they try too hard for others — and I would like such people, above all, to keep a quiet observation point at hand for keeping themselves sustainable.

articles.title: Affirming the luxury of doing nothing. Rich time on an unfilled day off, spent with cards and coffee
articles.summary: On days off, don't you end up packing your schedule even more than on weekdays — going out to popular events, having lunch with friends, and clearing away the housework that has piled up?

blocks.text: On days off, don't you end up packing your schedule even more than on weekdays — going out to popular events, having lunch with friends, and clearing away the housework that has piled up?

Unconsciously pushing yourself to have a fulfilling day off, you end up completely using up your energy by Sunday night. Among modern people like that, the value of the "luxury of doing nothing" — deliberately spending the day with a blank schedule — is now being reconsidered.
Keeping your schedule blank, and only widening the depth of your heart, on a day off
That said, when you actually leave a day off unscheduled, you tend to end up idly checking work email on your smartphone, or lazily scrolling social media and feeling guilty.
The trick to truly savoring a "day off doing nothing" is to prepare just one "quiet pleasure" — like taking a small journey inward, instead of going out.
An afternoon with a favorite drink, turning through 78 stories
On an afternoon of a day off with no plans, with a carefully brewed coffee or tea in hand, I open DECIDE.. I really enjoy spending time that way.

There is no need to rush to make a decision. You might draw a single card and gaze at the current state of your heart, or open the page listing all 78 cards and slowly lose yourself in reading the beautiful world of symbols and the "hints for when you're unsure," like a collection of essays.
Without going anywhere, and without spending money, your own thinking grows deep and clear. Why not experience such a thoughtful, calm day off this coming weekend?

articles.title: What doesn't change, even in an age of rapid change. DECIDE, a place where classic tarot and the latest digital meet
articles.summary: In an age where tools and ways of working that were common sense a few years ago quickly become outdated, and new technologies and values arrive year after year. Living in such a fast-changing era, "From here on, what should I rely on to make my judgments…"

blocks.text: In an age where tools and ways of working that were common sense a few years ago quickly become outdated, and new technologies and values arrive year after year. Living in such a fast-changing era, there are moments when you feel uneasy, wondering, "From here on, what should I rely on to make my judgments?"

But no matter how much the outside world and technology evolve, there is just one thing that hasn't changed at all for hundreds, thousands of years. That is the structure of the heart: "what people feel unsure about, what they rejoice in, and how they overcome their uncertainty."
"Human wisdom" passed down for hundreds of years, brought into life today

The 78 tarot cards are, so to speak, a "crystallization of humanity's wisdom," systematizing those universal movements of the human heart. Far from becoming outdated, their essential perspectives shine all the more brightly precisely in a modern age of intense, complex change.
And DECIDE. is what removed the dubious occult elements from that classical wisdom and elevated it into the minimal digital space that is easiest for those of us living today to use.
A home for your thinking, where you can always return when you're unsure

The experience of drawing a card and gaining a perspective, a log function for engraving your own thoughts, and a statistics function for learning your own patterns. In this place, both old and new, everything is in place for you to keep standing on "your own feet," without being swallowed by the great waves of the times.

No matter how noisily the world changes, when you open this place, you can always return to your quiet self. I would be glad if you would place DECIDE. beside your everyday life as such a home ground for your thinking.
